To: docs/climate-programme/border-revenues-launch/handover
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: DRAFT — Thursday launch handover for Inês

DRAFT — for me to read on the train before sharing.

Inês,

My father is ill, I am with my family. I don’t yet know how long I will be away. I’m asking you to take Thursday’s launch without me, and I’m sorry to leave you with a correction and a change of speaker this late.

I trust you completely. You know this paper as well as I do, and you ran the annex B sensitivity runs yourself. You do not need to stand up there and try to sound like me. Present it in your own way and use your judgement. I’ve put the urgent things first below so you don’t have to reconstruct them from my inbox.

1. First priority: get the corrected number to Hanna and into the slides

The correct estimate for 2030 LDC-relevant revenue is EUR 1.4 billion, not EUR 2.1 billion. Figure 3 and the summary were using the old run, which did not apply the free allocation phase-out. The conclusion of the paper does not change, but the headline number does. We need to be clear about both parts, not make the correction sound smaller than it is.

Current state:
- PDF v7 on the drive is corrected on pages 3, 14 and 15. Use this version for the launch and any further circulation.
- Deck v4 is NOT corrected: slides 6 and 9 need fixing. Slide 9 contains the revenue chart. Please check the speaker notes too; my old notes are still in there.
- The embargoed press release is NOT corrected. Hanna sent it to 34 Brussels contacts on Friday with the EUR 2.1 billion figure.

Please contact Hanna first and ask her to arrange a corrected release and an explicit correction to everyone who received the original. The embargo lifts Thursday 26 November at 10:00 CET, so this needs handling before then, with enough time for journalists to amend anything already drafted. Ask her to make clear that the corrected release supersedes Friday’s version, and to use PDF v7 for any accompanying paper.

Geert knows I am away and can sign off a corrected press release if Hanna needs a senior name. Please go straight to him rather than waiting for me.

A straightforward correction line would be:

“The estimate for 2030 LDC-relevant revenue is EUR 1.4 billion, rather than EUR 2.1 billion. The earlier figure came from a model run that did not apply the free allocation phase-out. The paper’s conclusion is unchanged; the headline revenue estimate has been corrected.”

The 2.1 mistake is mine, not yours. Say that if anyone asks. You should not have to take responsibility for it because you are the person presenting. There is no need to be evasive or protective of me.

Once the release is being dealt with, correct the deck against PDF v7 and check that the chart, labels, summary figures and notes all agree. Before anything goes out or goes on screen, do one final check that we are using the corrected PDF and corrected slides.

2. Confirm the speaker change and revised running order with Tomás

The run-of-show document is out of date. Tomás emailed this morning: Lindqvist has a vote and must leave at 13:30. He asked for a 15-minute presentation and a 12:50 panel start, and she wants to take at least two questions herself before leaving.

Please tell Tomás you will replace me for the presentation and panel, and confirm the revised timings with him. The working schedule is:

- 12:00: guests at the security entrance; Tomás collects badges. Light lunch is available outside the room from 12:00.
- 12:30: Lindqvist’s welcome, five minutes.
- 12:35–12:50: your presentation, 15 minutes.
- 12:50: panel with you, Dr. Abena Owusu-Mensah and Florian Kessler, moderated by Lindqvist until she leaves.
- Before 13:30: space for at least two audience questions with Lindqvist.
- 13:30: Lindqvist leaves.
- 14:00: close.

The original plan had Q&A starting at 13:40, which no longer covers her request. Please agree with Tomás how to bring questions forward and, importantly, who moderates after 13:30. That is not settled in the material I have.

The venue remains the European Parliament, Altiero Spinelli building, in the room booked by Lindqvist’s office.

Hard deadline: Tomás needs the final names from our side by Wednesday 25 November at 12:00. He says security will not admit people otherwise. Make sure your name is on the final list and confirm any other institute attendees. Ask him to update the speaker details wherever needed.

3. Prepare for 15 minutes, not 20

Deck v4 has 14 slides. Please cut or skip whatever you need to give the argument room in 15 minutes; you do not owe my speaker notes any loyalty.

Lead with the paper’s question and main finding, explain the corrected revenue estimate plainly, and leave enough time for what it means for LDCs and the recommendations. I would not let either the correction or Kessler’s preferred debate consume the presentation.

Abena’s remote link is in the calendar invite. Your deck note says she tested it successfully. Please make sure she knows you are presenting and that the panel now starts at 12:50, and arrange a quick connection check with whoever is running the room. She was strong on the LDC side in our call; give her room to make her own case rather than assuming she will defend ours.

And remember Lisbon: when the projector died at the COP side event, you rescued my panel. You are better live than you think. A shorter slot and a difficult question do not change that.

4. Wednesday press calls: confirm with Hanna, don’t assume

Hanna told two journalists I would be available Wednesday afternoon: one from a trade newsletter and one from a Belgian daily. The calendar has Wednesday 25 November at 14:00 and 15:00, 20 minutes each by phone, but the entry says “Hanna to confirm”.

Please ask Hanna to confirm the bookings and contacts, tell them about the speaker change, and arrange for you to take the calls if you can. If that makes the preparation unmanageable, ask her to rearrange rather than trying to squeeze everything in. Make sure both journalists have the correction before the calls.

The same factual line on EUR 1.4 billion should be used in the release, calls and presentation. The calls are before the embargo lifts; Hanna should confirm the embargo terms with them.

5. Kessler: answer the point, but don’t let him set the tone

He has already said he will raise the 80% pass-through assumption and resource shuffling. Neither is a surprise, and you know the sensitivity work first-hand.

On pass-through:
“80% is the central case, not the only case we tested. Annex B also runs 60% and 40%. The result holds at 60% and weakens at 40%.”

Say the last part openly. We should not imply that the result is equally strong under every assumption, or dismiss his concern about small manufacturers. Answer it, explain the sensitivity, then return to the paper’s wider question about revenues and LDCs. The panel should not become a referendum on one parameter.

On resource shuffling: we agree it is a risk, discuss it in section 5.2, and recommend the Commission’s monitoring report. Acknowledge that directly rather than treating it as an objection we forgot.

Keep those methodological questions separate from the figure 3 correction. The revenue error came from the old run’s treatment of free allocation; it is not an annex B error.

6. Small follow-up that needs arranging before the event

Lucy Tran from Halvorsen is attending with a colleague. For the grant report she needs two event photos and attendance numbers, ideally by 4 December.

Please ask someone in advance to take the photos and record attendance so you are not trying to do it while presenting. Confirm with Hanna or Tomás who can cover this and collect the material afterwards for Lucy.

If you need me

You can call me. After 09:00 tomorrow, Tuesday 24 November, I might not pick up, so please do not make reaching me a condition for getting things done. Use Geert for senior sign-off, Hanna for press arrangements and Tomás for Parliament logistics.

If anyone asks why I’m away, the only explanation I want shared is: “My father is ill, I am with my family.” Nothing further.

I’m sorry about the mistake and about leaving you to sort it out at such short notice. I know this is extra work, not just a change of name on the programme. Thank you for taking it on. I trust your judgement on the paper, the room and what needs to give if time gets tight.

Marieke
